title: Opportunistic mini-batches, KV prioritization, and smart degradation for OOM resilience
creator: Priya Menon
description: Goal: reduce tail OOMs and improve recovery latency for high-concurrency serving workloads by combining small opportunistic batch formation, priority-aware KV cache retention, and a lightweight degradation protocol that preserves useful output. This ticket prototypes an admission-and-shedding pipeline that: (1) forms mini-batches below the normal batch window for short-lived latency-sensitive requests; (2) assigns KV retention priorities per request using recency, semantic score, and explicit customer hints; (3) triggers a multi-tiered degradation path (compact-KV, partial-output, model-fallback) when GPU headroom drops below thresholds. Deliverables: design doc, prototype scheduler, unit+integration tests, perf canary, rollout plan. Motivations: current tail OOMs occur during odd event spikes where large KV working sets plus bursty long-sequence requests cause immediate memory pressure. Pure eviction policies cause quality cliffs — this approach aims to reduce cliff severity and increase successful request fraction.
decision_notes: 02-18: Choose mini-batch window of 5-20ms (configurable); default 10ms after perf sweep — tradeoff between latency and aggregation benefit.
02-22: Prioritization vector will include: last_access_ts, semantic_hot_score (from LRU + embedding delta), explicit customer pin; normalized into 0-1 retention weight.

02-25: Degradation ladder decided: 1) compact-KV (lossy compression via 8-bit delta quantization on cold keys), 2) prefix-dropping (emit partial response and ask client to retry with continuation token), 3) model-fallback to smaller-ctx variant, 4) soft-reject with NACK. We prioritized options that preserve partial output over silent truncation.
03-01: Will instrument token-level quality metrics for canary: BLEU-like deltas on sampled prompts and a ‘meaningful-answer’ binary classifier to detect regressions.
03-03: Opted to keep security_review_required=false for now; fallback telemetry will not include PII and K/V keys are hashed before logging.
updates: 2026-02-12: Initial spike analysis attached — saw 3.4x increase in OOMs during a marketing event; root cause correlated with long-seq prompts and warm KV churn.
2026-02-16: Prototype scheduler implemented in the admission-controller; supports mini-batch timers and per-request priority token. Basic unit tests pass.
2026-02-20: KV retention scoring algorithm POC added to runtime: score = 0.6*recency + 0.3*semantic_hot + 0.1*customer_pin; tuning pending.
2026-02-24: First perf run on a p4d-like node: mini-batching reduced per-token compute by 8% but increased median latency by 6ms; acceptable for high-priority requests at default config.
2026-02-28: Design review with PM and Design finished; requested clearer UX signals for clients when partial outputs are returned (continuation token + suggested retry).
2026-03-02: Integration test with KV compacting implemented; end-to-end canary shows 45% reduction in hard OOMs on synthetic workload with spike profile.
2026-03-05: Preparing canary config and rollout plan; need approvals for runtime-1.20 canary window.
acceptance_criteria: Canary run (1% traffic) for 72h shows <10% increase in request-level latency and >30% reduction in hard OOMs compared to baseline.
No customer-facing silent truncations: all degraded responses include explicit continuation tokens or fallbacks with clear client signals.
Automated unit and integration tests for admission, KV scoring, and compact-KV pass in CI; PRs linked and merged.
Dashboard panels (per-route OOMs, degraded-response-rate, mean recovery latency) created in Console and alerted when thresholds breached.
Rollout playbook documented: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full, with rollback triggers and mitigation runbooks.
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521 - admission-controller: mini-batch timer and priority token
testing_notes: Stress harness: replayed production traces with injected 2x spike; added synthetic long-seq generator to exercise KV churn.
Quality scoring: sample set of 2k prompts used to compute meaningful-answer deltas before/after degradation.
Chaos tests: simulate GPU memory fragmentation and ensure degradation ladder triggers and recovers without deadlocks.
rollout_plan: Canary: runtime-1.20 canary pool, 1% traffic for 72h with enhanced telemetry.
Stage: 10% traffic for 48h, monitor latency and degraded-response-rate; allow manual rollback.
Wider: 50% then opt-in to full if metrics stable for 7d; add client-facing SDK opt-in flag for early adopters.
